audit_findings.title: The earnings numerator and June 2026 claim perimeter do not match
audit_findings.magnitude: valuation error unquantified; H1 2026 acquisition Adjusted EBITDA contributions were $47.7 million ($40.2 million Micromax and $7.5 million EFC), while MGS reduced comparable H1 Adjusted EBITDA by $5.3 million
audit_findings.mechanism: The OE anchor excludes post-closing EFC and Micromax earnings while the cash, debt, contingent claims and share denominator are dated after those acquisitions; it also includes partial-period MGS earnings from a divested business.
audit_findings.evidence: However, EFC will be reported in the Specialties segment and Micromax will be reported in the Electronics segment beginning in the first quarter of 2026.
audit_findings.explanation: This is a demonstrated perimeter error, not merely a forecasting risk. Missing acquisition earnings tends to understate value, while retained MGS earnings and post-acquisition financing or seller claims without matching costs tend to overstate it. The filed operating contributions are material relative to the $179.5 million anchor, but the net common-equity OE correction cannot be established from EBITDA alone.
audit_findings.action: Construct post-closing trailing owner earnings that remove MGS and include EFC and Micromax earnings, taxes, working capital, maintenance capex, interest, NCI and contingent consideration; align the bridge and 248.77107 million-share denominator to that same date and rerun all scenarios.

audit_findings.title: Incremental acquisition interest is absent from the equity-level anchor
audit_findings.magnitude: $18.3 million higher interest expense, net, in H1 2026 versus H1 2025; acquisition-specific recurring after-tax amount unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Because this is an equity-level OE DCF, recurring after-tax interest on the February 2026 term loans and revolver must reduce OE rather than being handled through a debt-principal deduction.
audit_findings.evidence: This acquisition was funded with the proceeds from the Add-on Term Loans of $ 450 million, which closed simultaneously with the Micromax Acquisition, and borrowings under the Company's revolving credit facility.
audit_findings.explanation: The timing mismatch is demonstrated: the $179.5 million FY2025 anchor predates the acquisition financing, while the June 2026 bridge includes $2,119.4 million of debt. The filed six-month increase in net interest equals 10.2% of the anchor, although the filing attributes it jointly to higher debt, lower interest income and revolver borrowing. That scale is reasonably capable of materially changing the valuation.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile each June 2026 debt balance to its effective rate, hedge cash flows and interest income; calculate the recurring after-tax acquisition-financing cost, insert it into the aligned post-closing OE numerator and rerun all scenarios.

audit_findings.title: Kuprion milestone consideration is a material unmodeled senior claim
audit_findings.magnitude: up to $250.2 million remaining after filed $3.9 million and $4.9 million milestone payments; equivalent to $1.01 per diluted share and 9.2% of base equity value
audit_findings.mechanism: Expected milestone payments reduce cash available to common owners or require a separate bridge deduction when Kuprion-related earnings and growth are included.
audit_findings.evidence: On May 19, 2023, the Company completed the Kuprion Acquisition for $ 15.9 million, net of cash, with potential additional payments in various installments, which are not to exceed $ 259 million in aggregate, to be made upon the achievement of certain milestones associated with product qualification and revenue through December 31, 2030.
audit_findings.explanation: The contractual contingent-payment structure is demonstrated, although the amount likely to be paid remains unresolved. The remaining contractual maximum is large relative to the $2,712 million base equity value and exceeds the $189.6 million cash bridge. Milestones were achieved in both 2024 and 2025, so treating the claim as immaterial without probability evidence is not supportable.
audit_findings.action: Obtain the milestone schedule, qualification and revenue thresholds, payment form and probability assessment; match forecast Kuprion benefits with expected payments or a probability-weighted bridge claim, then rerun the valuation.

audit_findings.title: Metals hedge losses require separate cash and noncash treatment
audit_findings.magnitude: $47.2 million FY2025 loss comprising $30.5 million realized and $16.7 million unrealized; respectively 17.0% and 9.3% of the $179.5 million anchor
audit_findings.mechanism: Realized hedge losses are operating cash costs that reduce OE, while unrealized marks should not reduce current cash OE but must be reconciled to later settlements without double counting.
audit_findings.evidence: Other expense, net for 2025 included $47.2 million of net losses associated with metals derivative contracts ($30.5 million of realized and $16.7 million of unrealized losses), $3.6 million of charges due to highly inflationary accounting for our operations in Turkey and $1.8 million of debt extinguishment costs related to the partial prepayment of our term loans B-3 in the first quarter of 2025.
audit_findings.explanation: The filed components and their economic roles are established, but the supplied OE reconciliation does not show their treatment. Removing realized losses would overstate value; retaining a noncash unrealized loss in cash OE would understate it. Either component is large enough relative to the anchor to be material.
audit_findings.action: Trace the $179.5 million anchor line by line to net income, operating cash flow and hedge settlements; retain the $30.5 million realized operating loss, reverse only the $16.7 million noncash mark where appropriate, and rerun if the existing treatment differs.

audit_findings.title: Cross-currency swap liabilities may be an omitted claim ahead of common
audit_findings.magnitude: $39.3 million net liability at June 30, 2026, equal to $0.16 per diluted share and 1.45% of the $2,712 million base equity value
audit_findings.mechanism: A genuine net settlement exposure could require a bridge deduction, but the swaps also hedge euro net investments and convert term loans into euro-denominated fixed-rate exposure, so the liability cannot be assessed independently of the offset.
audit_findings.evidence: The fair value of the cross-currency swaps was a net liability of $ 64.7 million at December 31, 2025 and a net asset of $ 54.0 million at December 31, 2024.
audit_findings.explanation: The latest filing resolves the balance at the valuation date: the net liability declined from $64.7 million at December 2025 to $39.3 million at June 2026. Even an unsupported full deduction would reduce base value only from $10.90 to approximately $10.74 per share and would not change the valuation conclusion. The economic direction remains unknown because the offsetting euro exposure was not quantified.
audit_findings.action: Document the June 2026 gross swap assets and liabilities, settlement terms and offsetting euro net investment; no rerun is needed unless that net-exposure analysis identifies an economic claim materially exceeding the filed $39.3 million fair value.

audit_findings.title: The FY2025 anchor may capitalize temporary cash drains as permanent weakness
audit_findings.magnitude: $72.2 million filed decline in FY2025 operating cash flow, equal to 40.2% of the $179.5 million anchor; sustainable adjustment unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Temporary working-capital movements, prior-year incentive payments and nonrecurring transaction payments depress the starting OE that is compounded and capitalized in every scenario.
audit_findings.evidence: The decrease in net cash flows provided by operating activities of $72.2 million was primarily driven by higher working capital investment, higher incentive compensation payments that were associated with 2024 performance, lower earnings as a result of the MGS Transaction and higher payments associated with transaction expenses.
audit_findings.explanation: The cash-flow decline and identified causes are filed facts, but it is unresolved how much is temporary versus a recurring requirement. The entire $72.2 million is not a valid add-back because it also includes lower MGS earnings and potentially normal compensation, acquisition and growth costs. Nevertheless, its scale relative to the anchor makes normalization reasonably capable of materially changing value.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile the anchor to cash-flow statement lines and payment timing; separate recurring working capital, compensation and acquisition costs from reversals and genuinely nonrecurring payments, calculate normalized post-perimeter OE and rerun all scenarios.
